steps.text: This time the test itself is wrong. Watch how born-green handles it.

steps.desc: Provider: get_config("nonexistent") returns "" (empty string). Correct behavior.

steps.highlight: line 22: wrong assert — expects "default", actual is ""
steps.desc: Look at line 22: it expects get_config("nonexistent") == "default", but the code returns "". This test cannot pass.

steps.text: Try to register the guarantee. GBC runs the test immediately — if it fails, registration is refused. That is born-green.

steps.desc: Register guarantee — wrong test; should be refused

args.desc: get_config(key) always returns str, never None.

steps.text:
Registration refused.

Born-green means you cannot install a failing guarantee, let alone ship changes on top of it. GBC does not only catch breaks after edits — it also ensures the test is honest at registration time.

First line of defense: not "break then discover", but "a bad test never enters the graph".
